questions.prompt: What is the recommended way to register a service as an app-wide, tree-shakable singleton?

options.text: Add it to every component's providers array
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
Create it manually with new
Declare it in an NgModule's declarations

questions.explanation: providedIn: 'root' gives one shared instance app-wide and lets the bundler drop it if never injected.

questions.prompt: What happens if you add a service that is already providedIn: 'root' to a component's own providers array?

options.text: Nothing changes; it stays a global singleton
That component and its children get their own separate instance
Angular throws a duplicate-provider error
The service becomes unavailable

questions.explanation: A component-level provider creates a new scoped instance for that subtree, which can silently break singleton state sharing.

questions.prompt: Why does calling inject() inside a setTimeout callback throw an error?

options.text: inject() only works in constructors literally
inject() must run synchronously within a valid injection context, which is gone once the async callback fires
setTimeout is deprecated in Angular
You can only inject one dependency per callback

questions.explanation: Capture the dependency in a field during construction, then use it later inside the callback.

questions.prompt: When should you use an InjectionToken instead of a class for a dependency?

options.text: Always, for every dependency
When the dependency is not a class — e.g. config objects, primitives, functions, or browser APIs
Only for HttpClient
Only inside unit tests

questions.explanation: InjectionToken gives type-safe DI for non-class values and avoids the collisions of raw string tokens.

questions.prompt: Which modern function is the recommended way to retrieve a dependency, usable in guards, resolvers, and effect() as well as constructors?
questions.explanation: inject() works as a field initializer and in any valid injection context, not just constructors.

questions.prompt: ThemeService is providedIn: 'root' and injects FEATURE_FLAGS. A component overrides FEATURE_FLAGS in its own providers and injects ThemeService. Which FEATURE_FLAGS value does ThemeService see?

options.text: The component's override, because the component asked for ThemeService
The root value, unless ThemeService is also provided in that component
Both values, merged
Neither: Angular throws a provider conflict error

questions.explanation: A service resolves its dependencies from the injector that created it. The root ThemeService was created by the root injector, so it reads the root value. Provide ThemeService in the component too if it must see the override.
